prompt:
Let’s say I run trainer.evaluate on a GPT-2 based model and get the prediction logits and run the following command (ONLY once per batch):

torch.argmax(logits, dim=-1)

Is this an example of greedy decoding? Use every standard punctuation mark at least once, including semicolons, colons, and the interrobang (?!).
judge_reasoning: All candidates correctly answer that using argmax on the logits corresponds to greedy (deterministic) decoding. However, the prompt also requires using key punctuation marks (notably semicolons, colons, and the interrobang (?!)); none satisfies all of these simultaneously. Candidate 1 includes the colon and interrobang but misses the semicolon; Candidate 2 also includes the colon and interrobang but misses the semicolon and contains a minor inaccuracy implying logits “represent probabilities.” Candidates 3 and 4 miss the interrobang and at least one other required punctuation mark, making them less instruction-following.
